questions.q: When did each division of the army serve?
questions.a: Each division served for one month so that there were always workers on duty throughout the year.

questions.q: How many men were in each division of the army?
questions.a: There were 24,000 men in each division.

questions.q: Who commanded the divisions that served throughout the year?
questions.a: Each month a different commander served and had authority over the commanders of all the divisions on duty that month.

questions.q: Who were the leaders of the tribes of Reuben and Simeon?
questions.a: Eliezer, the son of Zichri, was the leader of Reuben, and Shephatiah, the son of Maacah, was the leader of Simeon.

questions.q: Who were the leaders of the tribe of Levi and of Aaron’s descendants?
questions.a: Hashabiah, the son of Kemuel, was the leader of the tribe of Levi, and Zadok was the leader of Aaron’s descendants, the priests.

questions.q: Who were the leaders of the tribes of Judah and Issachar?
questions.a: Elihu, one of David’s brothers, was the leader of Judah, and Omri, the son of Michael, was the leader of Issachar.

questions.q: Who were the leaders of the tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali?
questions.a: Ishmaiah, the son of Obadiah, was the leader of Zebulun, and Jerimoth, the son of Azriel, was the leader of Naphtali.

questions.q: Who were the leaders of the tribe of Ephraim and the western half of Manasseh?
questions.a: Hoshea, the son of Azaziah, was the leader of Ephraim, and Joel, the son of Pedaiah, was the leader of the western half of Manasseh.

questions.q: Who were the leaders of the eastern half of Manasseh and the tribe of Benjamin?
questions.a: Iddo, the son of Zechariah, was the leader of the eastern half of Manasseh in Gilead, and Jaasiel, the son of Abner, was the leader of Benjamin.

questions.q: Who was the leader of the tribe of Dan?
questions.a: Azarel, the son of Jeroham, was the leader of Dan.

questions.q: Why did David not count those twenty years old or younger?
questions.a: He did not count them because Yahweh had promised to increase Israel like the stars of the heavens.

questions.q: What happened when Joab tried to count the men of Israel?
questions.a: He started to count them, but he did not finish, because Yahweh was angry with Israel about it, and the record of King David’s reign does not include the number.

questions.q: Over what was Jonathan son of Uzziah responsible?
questions.a: He was over the storehouses in the fields, in the cities, in the villages, and in the towers.

questions.q: Who was in charge of the workers who farmed the king’s land?
questions.a: Ezri, the son of Chelub, was in charge of them.

questions.q: Who was in charge of the vineyards, and who was in charge of storing the wine?
questions.a: Shimei the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards, and Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of storing the wine.

questions.q: Who was in charge of the groves and who was in charge of storing the oil?
questions.a: Baal Hanan of Geder was in charge of the groves of olive and sycamore trees, and Joash was in charge of storing the olive oil.

questions.q: Who was in charge of the herds in Sharon, and who was in charge of the herds in the valleys?
questions.a: Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the herds in Sharon, and Shaphat, the son of Adlai, was in charge of the herds in the valleys.

questions.q: Who was in charge of the camels, and who was in charge of the donkeys?
questions.a: Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels, and Jehdeiah the Meronothite was in charge of the donkeys.

questions.q: Who was in charge of the flock?
questions.a: Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the flock.

questions.q: Why was Jonathan, David’s uncle, an advisor?
questions.a: He was an advisor, since he was a wise man and a scribe.

questions.q: Who was the king’s advisor, and who was the king’s friend?
questions.a: Ahithophel was the king’s advisor, and Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend.

questions.q: Who became the king’s advisors after Ahithophel, and who was the commander of the king’s army?
questions.a: Jehoiada, the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar became advisors after Ahithophel, and Joab was the commander of the king’s army.

commentary.text: Verses 1–15 In the kingdoms of this world readiness for war forms a security for peace; in like manner, nothing so much encourages Satan's assaults as to be unwatchful. So long as we stand armed with the whole armour of God, in the exercise of faith, and preparation of heart for the conflict, we shall certainly be safe, and probably enjoy inward peace.

The officers of the court, or the rulers of the king's substance, had the oversight and charge of the king's tillage, his vineyards, his herds, his flocks, which formed the wealth of eastern kings. Much of the wisdom of princes is seen in the choice of their ministry, and common persons show it in the choice of their advisers. David, though he had all these about him, preferred the word of God before them all. Thy testimonies are my delight and my counsellors.
